title: Seventh Word Interpreting The Comparison Death Belief Patience And Reliance

questions.question: In this passage, who does the unfortunate soldier stand for?
questions.answer: He stands for every human being, including the person’s own self.

questions.question: What does the lion represent?
questions.answer: It represents a person’s appointed time to die.

questions.question: What does the gallows represent in the comparison?
questions.answer: It represents death, fading away, and being separated from loved ones.

questions.question: What do the two wounds stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for human weakness and human neediness.

questions.question: What does the long journey represent?
questions.answer: It represents the long path of human life and what comes after it, from before birth all the way to resurrection.

questions.question: What are the two talismans explained in the passage?
questions.answer: They are belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: How does belief in the Hereafter change the meaning of death for a believer?
questions.answer: It turns death into a way to go from this world to the beauty and mercy of the next life.

questions.question: Why do some wise people welcome death, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because they understand that it can lead a believer to a better place with Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah change the way a person sees passing time and loss?
questions.answer: It helps the person see changes in life as signs of Allah’s power, mercy, and beautiful creation.

questions.question: What picture is used to help explain how changing things can still be beautiful?
questions.answer: The passage uses the example of changing reflections and changing scenes that make new beauty appear.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak to the nafs in a serious way?
questions.answer: Because the nafs had once laughed carelessly but now feels sorrow and needs to learn the truth.

questions.question: In the comparison, what truth is given about the soldier?
questions.answer: The soldier is a picture of human life.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to friends through the passing of days and nights?
questions.answer: It says people part from one another and are lost through the changes of life.

questions.question: Which part of the comparison shows that people are not fully strong on their own?
questions.answer: The wound that stands for human weakness shows that.

questions.question: Which part of the comparison shows that people are always in need?
questions.answer: The wound that stands for poverty and need shows that.

questions.question: What stages are included in the long journey?
questions.answer: It includes the path from the world of spirits, to the womb, childhood, old age, the grave, the intermediate life, resurrection, and the bridge.

questions.question: What two beliefs are given as the answer to these fears?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Last Day.

questions.question: When a person believes in the Last Day, what does death become like?
questions.answer: It becomes like a ride carrying the believer out of this world to Paradise.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does this ride take the believer?
questions.answer: It takes the believer from the prison of this world to the gardens of Paradise and to Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah help a person think about change and endings?
questions.answer: It helps the person see them as chances to notice Allah’s amazing works and mercy.

questions.question: What idea do the changing mirror colors and moving scenes help explain?
questions.answer: They help explain that when things change, new and better beauties can appear.

questions.question: What is the first symbol explained in the passage, and what does it mean?
questions.answer: The soldier is explained first, and it means the human being.

questions.question: What danger does the lion point to?
questions.answer: It points to the nearness and certainty of death’s appointed time.

questions.question: What does the gallows teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: It teaches that life in this world includes death, change, and separation.

questions.question: Why are the two wounds described as serious?
questions.answer: Because human weakness and need are deep problems that people cannot fully solve by themselves.

questions.question: What does the passage show by describing life as a journey?
questions.answer: It shows that human life keeps moving through many stages and does not end at this world.

questions.question: What are believers given to face these problems?
questions.answer: They are given faith in Allah and the Hereafter.

questions.question: What change happens to death through belief in the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It is no longer seen as only an end, but as a way to reach a better eternal life.

questions.question: Why is this a comfort to believers?
questions.answer: Because it means death can bring them to peace, mercy, and Paradise.

questions.question: What does belief in Allah help a person notice in the world?
questions.answer: It helps the person notice Allah’s power, art, and mercy in the changing world.

questions.question: What does the Arabic sentence at the end of the passage mean in a simple way?
questions.answer: It means that we belong to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: Who is being addressed by the words to the nafs?
questions.answer: A person’s own self that needs correction and guidance.

questions.question: What is the purpose of explaining the soldier image?
questions.answer: The purpose is to show what human life is really like.

questions.question: What human experience is represented by the lion waiting nearby?
questions.answer: It represents the fixed time when death will come.

questions.question: What human experiences are gathered into the meaning of the gallows?
questions.answer: It includes death, growing weaker, and losing people through separation.

questions.question: What do the wounds teach us about ourselves?
questions.answer: They teach that people are weak and full of needs.

questions.question: Why is the journey described as very long?
questions.answer: Because it stretches across many parts of existence, not just our years in this world.

questions.question: What two beliefs are called talismans in this passage?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and faith in the life to come.

questions.question: How does the second talisman help with fear of death?
questions.answer: It makes death seem like a servant that carries the believer to a beautiful destination.

questions.question: What does the passage say wise people understood about death?
questions.answer: They understood its true meaning, so they did not only fear it.

questions.question: How does the first talisman change the meaning of separation and passing time?
questions.answer: It turns them into ways of seeing Allah’s wonderful works again and again.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention new scenes appearing when old ones change?
questions.answer: To show that change can reveal fresh beauty instead of only loss.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the soldier teach us about ourselves?
questions.answer: He teaches that every person faces danger, weakness, and a long journey.

questions.question: What does the lion symbolize that no one can escape forever?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the moment of death appointed for each person.

questions.question: What does the gallows symbolize about worldly life?
questions.answer: It symbolizes that people and things do not remain forever and that separation comes.

questions.question: What is meant by the first wound?
questions.answer: It means people do not have endless strength or power.

questions.question: What is meant by the second wound?
questions.answer: It means people have many needs and cannot provide everything for themselves.

questions.question: What does the exile-like journey show about human existence?
questions.answer: It shows that life moves through many stages toward the next world.

questions.question: What are the two spiritual keys given in this section?
questions.answer: They are belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What happens to the image of death when a person believes in the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It changes from something frightening into a means of reaching Paradise.

questions.question: According to the passage, why might wise people long for death?
questions.answer: Because they see it as a meeting with mercy and a passage to something better.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah change the way a person sees the world’s constant changes?
questions.answer: It helps the person see those changes as displays of Allah’s creative beauty and mercy.

questions.question: What do the examples of reflections and picture-like scenes help the reader understand?
questions.answer: They help the reader understand that renewed change can bring new beauty.

questions.question: What is one main point of the passage’s explanation of the soldier story?
questions.answer: It explains that the story is really about the condition of human beings.

questions.question: What part of the story stands for a person’s final time in this world?
questions.answer: The lion stands for that final appointed time.

questions.question: What part stands for death and the loss of loved ones over time?
questions.answer: The gallows stands for those things.

questions.question: What do the two wounds reveal about human nature?
questions.answer: They reveal that people are weak and needy.

questions.question: What does the long road in the comparison include beyond this world?
questions.answer: It includes the grave, the intermediate life, resurrection, and the bridge.

questions.question: What two beliefs are presented as the answer to fear and confusion?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: How is death described after a person has faith in the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It is described like a controlled ride carrying the believer to goodness.

questions.question: What place is this ride leading toward?
questions.answer: It is leading toward Paradise and Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Why is this understanding important for a believer?
questions.answer: Because it brings comfort and removes hopelessness.

questions.question: How does faith in Allah affect the way a person sees loss, endings, and passing days?
questions.answer: It helps the person see them as signs of Allah’s ongoing wisdom, power, and mercy.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of things being replaced by better scenes?
questions.answer: The lesson is that change does not only take away; it can also uncover greater beauty.
